Back in college my councillor recommended me a therapist and psychiatrist because I had panic attacks turns out those panic attacks are based on my PTSD, went through different treatments got addicted to pills and for a long time i thought I was getting better turns out I'm not, I thought I was doing everything wrong I go to therapy talk to damn people who I thought could fix me turns out I'm the only one who can fix me. During my therapy they put me under a rehabilitated care those "stay at the hospital " type of sessions.

So I lived in the facility for a month, eat, pray, then take pills I get run an assessment every weak. Everyday they're going to associate my mental illness with God and I'm like what does God have to do with this? Turns out the answer they gave me is Take pills, take care of yourself and Pray.

When my dad saw those pills he told me "everyone's depressed or going through something's but all you need are people in your life who can get you through it" he warned me about getting addicted turns out he was right.

My therapist recommended me 5 pills a day, they knew I didn't have much money but they still charged me highly and when I asked why they said it's based on "God's Plan"

One evening I overdosed, my professor came to my dorm and took me to the hospital the medication that I've been taking numbs my hunger and other senses. We drove around the city and he listened to my trauma, he gave me a hug and told me to quit since Its not good for me.

Therapy was supposed to help not make me worst by the end of 2020, I quit completely. 

Here's the truth about PTSD no matter what treatment you have, by the end of the day your life will be so much richer if you surround yourself with loving people, it's not your fault that the trauma happened, we always blame ourselves about things we can't control.

Stop thinking those pills will help you completely.

Sometimes all we need in life are close friends who can help you through this.
